content.title: RETIREMENT EXPERT: The SAFEST Way to Spend in Retirement | Wade Pfau on the 3 Income Paths
content.text: 00:00 Introduction – Retirement income expert Wade Pfau 01:27 Wade Pfau’s background in retirement income research 02:38 How retirement research changed Pfau’s thinking about the 4% rule 04:26 The biggest risks retirees face: longevity, market volatility, and spending shocks 06:39 The 3 major retirement income strategies explained 07:24 Strategy #1: Total return investing and the traditional 4% rule approach 11:19 Why most retirees don’t actually follow the 4% rule 13:28 Is the 4% rule still useful for retirement planning today? 15:28 Safe withdrawal rates in today’s interest rate environment 19:01 Strategy #2: The bucket strategy and managing sequence of returns risk 23:08 Do bonds still belong in a retirement portfolio? 26:18 Strategy #3: Income protection using annuities and guaranteed income 30:04 Understanding annuity fees and common misconceptions 34:26 Balancing lifetime income with legacy goals for heirs 41:41 How net worth and personality influence retirement income strategy 45:00 The retirement spending “smile” and how spending changes with age 47:38 Historical models vs real retiree behavior 1:00:01 The biggest financial and non-financial risks in retirement 1:04:15 Inflation risk and how retirees can protect their income 1:08:28 Where Social Security fits into a retirement income strategy 1:12:26 What to focus on five years before retirement 1:15:44 Big unanswered questions in retirement research 1:18:43 How Wade Pfau would structure his own retirement plan Retirement planning doesn’t end when you stop working — in many ways, the hardest financial decisions actually begin after you retire. In this conversation, retirement researcher Wade Pfau joins Erin to explain how to turn decades of savings into sustainable retirement income. If you’ve ever wondered how the 4% rule, safe withdrawal rates, annuities, Social Security claiming strategies, and investment portfolios fit together in retirement, this discussion walks through the research behind what works — and what many retirees misunderstand. Dr. Pfau has spent decades studying retirement income planning, sequence of returns risk, longevity risk, and retirement spending behavior. In this interview, he explains why retirement income strategies often need to go beyond simple rules of thumb and how retirees can design a financial plan that balances income stability, flexibility, and long-term portfolio growth. We explore three primary retirement income approaches commonly used by retirees and financial planners: • A total return investment strategy built around diversified portfolios and flexible withdrawals • A bucket strategy that segments assets for short-term spending and long-term growth • An income floor strategy using reliable income sources like Social Security Administration benefits, pensions, and annuities Along the way, Dr. Pfau explains how retirees can manage major financial risks in retirement, including market volatility, inflation risk, sequence risk, healthcare costs, and longevity risk. We also dive into some of the most debated topics in retirement planning today: • Whether the 4% rule still works in today’s market environment • How interest rates and bond yields influence safe withdrawal rates • When it may make sense to delay Social Security benefits • Why many retirees struggle psychologically to spend their savings You’ll also hear why many retirement researchers emphasize flexible spending strategies rather than rigid withdrawal rules, and how adjusting spending during market downturns can improve a retirement plan’s long-term success. If you’re approaching retirement or already retired, this conversation provides a research-driven look at how to build a sustainable retirement income strategy that supports both lifestyle spending and long-term financial security. Topics covered include: • Retirement income planning strategies • Safe withdrawal rates and the future of the 4% rule • Sequence of returns risk in retirement portfolios • Annuities vs bonds for retirement income • Social Security claiming strategies • Longevity risk and lifetime income planning Whether you’re building a retirement portfolio, evaluating annuity options, or deciding when to claim Social Security, this discussion provides valuable insights from one of the most respected voices in retirement research.
